open_points.subject: sandbox scratch-limit outcome
open_points.text: “the runner ignores the signal the host sends for a write past it, so the write fails with an error the code can see” and “a limit hit (memory, process count, scratch, `output_bytes`) — `resource_exhausted`”
open_points.question: How does `module:sandbox` reliably detect a write past the per-file scratch limit and return `resource_exhausted` when agent code catches the write error or replaces the ignored signal disposition?
options: The runner records every `SIGXFSZ` occurrence through a protected channel before agent code can handle it.
The parent detects an `RLIMIT_FSIZE` violation independently of the child process.
A caught write error is not considered a detected limit hit, so the execution may otherwise succeed.
open_points.default_guess: Have the runner record each `SIGXFSZ` occurrence through a protected channel and classify any recorded occurrence as `resource_exhausted`.
